parts:
Here’s a tighter, more emotionally intelligent, higher-converting version of your objections. These are built more around trust, authority, emotional buying psychology, consultative selling, and med spa owner realities instead of sounding “sales script-y.”

---

### Objection: “I need to talk to my partner/spouse/business partner/sister.”

:::writing{variant="standard" id="48271"}
“Absolutely. Honestly, I prefer that. These decisions impact the whole business, and I want them hearing everything directly instead of secondhand. Usually when someone tries to relay it later, important details get lost.

Let’s get a quick call on the calendar so everyone can ask questions, see the strategy, and make the best decision together. What’s the best email for them?”
:::

**Why this works better:**  
- Removes pressure  
- Positions you as collaborative, not defensive  
- Implies miscommunication happens without you saying “you won’t explain it right”  
- Keeps momentum by moving immediately to scheduling

---

### Objection: “I’m in a transition right now.”

:::writing{variant="standard" id="59384"}
“Honestly, that’s usually when our clients get the biggest wins.

Most owners wait until after the move, expansion, hire, or transition… and then they’re trying to build systems while already overwhelmed. We help you build the infrastructure before the chaos hits.

So instead of opening the new location still trying to figure out memberships, packages, retention, follow-up, and marketing… you walk in with it already working.

The goal is for your next chapter to launch with momentum instead of stress.”
:::

**Why this works better:**  
- Reframes timing as strategic  
- Creates fear of staying reactive  
- Feels advisory, not pushy  
- Speaks directly to owner exhaustion

---

### Objection: “I already have someone doing my marketing.”

:::writing{variant="standard" id="18462"}
“That’s completely fine. A lot of our clients do.

We’re not just a marketing company. Marketing is honestly one small piece of what we do. Most med spas don’t actually have a lead problem. They have a systems problem.

We look at the entire revenue journey:
• Follow-up  
• Consult conversions  
• Memberships  
• Packages  
• Retention  
• Client experience  
• Internal sales process  
• Lifetime value

If your current marketing team is great, amazing. We’ll make their job perform even better because now the backend is converting properly too.”
:::

**Why this works better:**  
- Doesn’t insult current vendor  
- Separates Luxora from “agency” category  
- Shifts focus from lead generation to revenue systems  
- Makes current marketing spend feel inefficient without backend optimization

---

### Objection: “How are you different from everyone else?”

:::writing{variant="standard" id="73195"}
“Most agencies are built to keep you dependent.

They run ads, send reports, lock you into contracts, and if you leave… everything falls apart because none of the knowledge was transferred to your team.

We built Luxora differently.

Yes, we help with marketing. But more importantly, we help you build a real revenue engine inside your business:
• Membership systems  
• Package architecture  
• Retention strategies  
• Follow-up automation  
• Front desk conversion  
• Client experience  
• Revenue optimization

And we teach your team how to actually operate it.

Our goal is not for you to need us forever. Our goal is for your business to become stronger, more profitable, and more predictable whether you stay with us or not.”
:::

**Why this works better:**  
- Strong positioning  
- Creates contrast without sounding bitter  
- Focuses on empowerment  
- Sounds premium and strategic

---

### Objection: “The pricing feels high.”

:::writing{variant="standard" id="26814"}
“I completely understand. And honestly, you should take investing in your business seriously.

What usually helps owners is looking at this less like a marketing expense and more like fixing the leaks already happening inside the business.

Most practices are sitting on a massive amount of unrealized revenue:
• Existing clients not returning  
• No memberships  
• Weak package structure  
• Poor follow-up  
• Underperforming consults  
• Untapped databases

That’s why our guarantee is tied to ROI, not deliverables.

Our goal is for this to pay for itself quickly through recovered and increased revenue, not become another monthly expense sitting on your P&L.”
:::

**Why this works better:**  
- Doesn’t instantly defend the price  
- Validates concern first  
- Repositions investment category  
- Avoids sounding “salesy guarantee bro”

---

### Objection: “Let me think about it.”

:::writing{variant="standard" id="91537"}
“Of course. This is a big decision and I’d rather you feel fully confident than rushed.

Can I ask… what specifically do you feel like you still need to think through?

Usually it’s one of a few things:
• Timing  
• Financial comfort  
• Trust/confidence  
• Team buy-in  
• Fear of another bad experience

I’d rather talk through it openly so I can give you clarity instead of you sitting with unanswered questions.

And either way, let’s put a quick follow-up on the calendar so you’re not starting from scratch later.”
:::

**Why this works better:**  
- Pulls out the *real* objection  
- Feels emotionally intelligent  
- Gives them permission to be honest  
- Keeps control of sales process without pressure

---

A few high-level sales tweaks that would dramatically improve close rates for Luxora specifically:

- Stop defending marketing. You are selling operational relief and predictable growth.
- Sell certainty, not leads.
- Med spa owners buy emotionally first, logically second.
- Most are exhausted, overwhelmed, burned by agencies, and scared of wasting money again.
- Your tone should feel: “experienced operator who understands the chaos,” not “agency salesperson.”
- Slow down on explaining features. Spend more time amplifying consequences of staying stuck.
- The best closers in aesthetics ask better questions instead of talking more.

Examples:
- “What happens if nothing changes in the next 12 months?”
- “How much revenue do you think is currently slipping through the cracks?”
- “What’s costing you more right now: the investment… or staying where you are?”
- “How long have you been trying to solve this already?”

That’s where emotional movement happens.
